findings.message: src/projects/CreatedFiles.tsx renders captured Markdown inline by default through src/document/Markdown.tsx. That component turns http(s) links into live external links and loads remote https images automatically (Markdown.tsx:28-36). So opening a launch node makes the browser fetch any https image URL in a file the worker wrote. That contradicts PRD section 2, which says 'links rendered as text or relative anchors only'. The file content is untrusted worker output and it is now shown unprompted, which makes this a new beacon surface. The ui lane was not allowed to edit Markdown.tsx, so the fix is a policy or follow-up decision: for captured files, either pass a component override or render images and external links as inert text.
findings.requirement: entries with a `file` artifact render inline for `.md` through `src/document/Markdown.tsx` (import it, do not modify it)

findings.message: src/projects/WorkerInputs.tsx: the task panel's required-check link used to scroll to and focus the executed check on the same page (#check-N). It now navigates to the verify_<lane> node and only carries data-check-index, so the reader lands at the top of the verify page instead of on the check. This is a small usability regression; the worker records it as an open assumption. inputs.spec.ts was changed to assert only the navigation.
findings.requirement: split `WorkerEvidence` in `src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx` into the produced view (result facts, created files, completion signal, launch receipt, task) for launch nodes and the verified view (result facts, checks with logs, gate and deferred checks, screenshots, other artifacts, ownership outcome) for verify nodes

findings.message: src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx VerifiedEvidence: the 'ownership outcome' text is inferred from phase and gate status ('the verifier checked the changed files against the lane's owned paths ... and the gate passed'), not taken from any served field. It is accurate for the current controller, but the viewer states it as a fact of the result. Consider wording it as derived, or serving the ownership check from the packet.

contracts/projects/examples.ts servedWorkerResult uses node_id 'verify_ui', and its doc comment points to '.../results/verify_ui/1'. The adapter actually serves worker results at results/<lane>/<attempt> (for example results/ui/1, as in server/projects.test.ts). This is cosmetic, but the example suggests a route that does not exist.

The [scenario:served-files] test (server/projects.test.ts:934) and the new malformed-files test (server/projects.test.ts:948) are never executed on the candidate. package.json test:unit does not list server/projects.test.ts, and the adapter lane's policy checks (workflow-unit, shared-contract, backend-regression, backend-build) contain no tsx run of that file. The candidate adapter packet shows only those four commands. The 37/37 pass exists only in the worker's summary. Part of the behaviour is still covered on the candidate: the candidate-phase browser suite serves seeded file artifacts through the real artifact route, and created-file-rendered asserts the exact .ts content and the legacy run. Nothing executed on the candidate asserts the text/plain content type, nosniff, or the RESULT_INVALID refusal. Add a backend-unit check that runs server/projects.test.ts to the viewer-clarity policy.

The six new browser scenarios have passed only in WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate. In the worker-phase ui packet (verification/worker/ui/1), the browser check failed with exit 1 before any test ran (ZodError on the missing file kind), and frontend-build and project-workflows-browser were deferred. The controller reruns only the candidate phase, and the candidate test report lists every scenario with the (candidate) suffix. So the fixture/mocked-route path of clarity.spec.ts has never passed against the real combined schema, only against the worker's scratch shim.
findings.requirement: asserting exactly what PRD section 6 lists, in both phases

findings.message: findings-by-reviewer asserts the group labels 'general · approved · …' and 'coverage · approved · …' (clarity.spec.ts:312-313). The only multi-reviewer runs it opens are RUN_FILES and RUN_TWO_REVIEWERS, and every reviewer in both approved, so the run verdict and each reviewer's own verdict are the same. A label that showed the combined run verdict instead of the reviewer's own would still pass. No test groups a run by reviewer where the reviewers' verdicts differ, for example RUN_REVIEWER_BLOCKED.
findings.requirement: groups in declared order labelled with the reviewer id, its verdict and severity counts
